column1: # Mutants this repository accepts as surviving, one per line:
#     class <TAB> method <TAB> what the mutator changed <TAB> why it is accepted
# This is the one place the arrangement is argued. The pom and CLAUDE.md name the gate and point here,
# because three copies of one argument are three things to keep in agreement.
# It replaces a surviving-mutant count. A count is satisfied by any set of the same size, so it cannot
# notice that one mutant was killed while another appeared. A list notices both, and the governance
# check also fails on an entry that is no longer alive, so this file cannot rot into a blanket exemption.
# The identity carries no line number on purpose: a line moves whenever anything above it is edited,
# and a file that needed regenerating after unrelated changes would stop being read.
# Every line carries a reason, and the reasons are of four kinds. Some mutants are provably equivalent,
# and the reason says why no input can tell them apart. Some are unobservable in a deterministic test -
# an interrupt flag restored for a caller that never checks it, teardown after the assertions are made,
# a failure path needing a fault injected at a chosen instant - and the reason says which. Some are
# redundant safety nets whose primary path is already covered. The remainder are cost judgements, and
# those say so plainly rather than claiming impossibility, because a reason you can disagree with is
# worth more than one that forecloses the argument.
# A reason beginning with [intermittent] marks a mutant whose outcome does not repeat. A teardown mutant
# is killed only when the scheduler lets a test observe the missing call, and every entry carrying the
# marker has been seen killed on one run and surviving on the next. The stale half of the check assumes
# an outcome that repeats, so without this marker a flapping mutant fails the build whichever way it
# is recorded, and a gate that is red either way stops being read. A marked entry is still checked as
# accepted, so a new survivor beside it is still caught, and only "this one is now killed, delete it"
# is suspended. That is a real cost - a marked line can rot into a permanent exemption - so the marker
# belongs only on an entry actually seen to flap, and never on one that is merely inconvenient to kill.
